result.summary: Ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs` for real (source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh; toolchain present): 41/44 passed, 3 failed. All 3 failures are in TEST-DESIGNER's own newly-split AC2 tests: 'AC2 level 2' (line 930), 'AC2 level 3' (line 948), 'AC2 level 4' (line 966). Each fails inside the insert_raw_event!/2 helper with `assert {:ok, event} = Repo.insert(changeset, ...)` matching `{:error, changeset}` -- the changeset carries `actor_id: {"can't be blank", [validation: :required]}`. Root cause: lib/letflow/event_store/event.ex declares :actor_id in @required_fields (line 112) and the events table's actor_id column is `null: false` at the DB level (priv/repo/migrations/20260816120001_create_events.exs:80) -- so `actor_id: nil` can never be persisted as a real event row in this schema. TEST-DESIGNER's gap-analysis explicitly states the restructuring deliberately changed levels 2-4 to pass `actor_id: nil` 'rather than an actor_id that merely fails to resolve' -- but that input is not constructible against the real schema, so 3 of the 5 restructured tests error out during fixture setup and never reach their assertion. Confirmed by diffing against the pre-restructuring version (git show b90a69b6:test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs): the original combined test used `actor_id: Ecto.UUID.generate()` (a real, syntactically valid but unresolvable UUID) for levels 2-4, which is why it passed (SECURITY-REVIEWER's recorded 40/40). The application logic itself (lib/letflow/instances.ex resolve_actor_display_name/3) is unaffected and correctly total for a nil actor_id -- this is purely a test-fixture defect introduced in this pass, not a regression in shipped code. Did not proceed to mutation testing since the baseline suite for the file under review does not pass -- mutation testing over a broken baseline would not produce a meaningful signal. Also checked and confirmed independently, all PASS: AC1's seed data has 4 genuinely distinct event_type values (INSTANCE_STARTED, INSTANCE_CANCELLED, INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND, TIMER_FIRED); AC6's test explicitly refutes both old field names (created_at, sequence_number) as well as asserting presence of the new ones; no @tag :skip/:pending or 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the file (grepped); every test uses its own TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 with a unique slug_prefix, no shared state; test/specs/REQ-200.md documents criterion/test-case/rationale for all 11 ACs correctly. These do not offset the blocking failure above -- FAIL immediately and completely per this role's own mandate.

issues.description: AC2 levels 2, 3 and 4 (test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs lines 930, 948, 966) pass `actor_id: nil` to insert_raw_event!/2. The events table's actor_id column is NOT NULL (priv/repo/migrations/20260816120001_create_events.exs:80) and Letflow.EventStore.Event.insert_changeset/2 lists :actor_id in @required_fields -- the insert changeset fails validation and `Repo.insert` returns `{:error, changeset}`, which the helper's `assert {:ok, event} = ...` then fails on. All 3 tests error at fixture setup, before their actor_display_name assertion ever runs. Fix: use `actor_id: Ecto.UUID.generate()` (a real, non-nil, unresolvable id) for these three levels, matching what the pre-restructuring combined test did and what a genuine 'no attributable actor' event actually looks like on this schema -- never a literal `nil`.
